# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

| **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts |

## 6. Severity classification

Classify every finding before writing outputs:

- **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed.
- **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge.
- **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge.

When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible.

### External-spec evidence rule

A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (for example, a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source does not contain when the reviewed code is behaviorally identical to it).

Without a verifiable citation:

- Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `<source>` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking."
- Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`.

This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force.

## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review

Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply.

- Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists.
- After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"*
- Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported.
- Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration.

## 8. Outputs

Write the standard review artifacts:

- `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts`
- `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment
- `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment

**Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments.

Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

## 9. Previously raised findings — the finding-identity registry

When `input/TICKET/pr_findings.md` is present, earlier review rounds on this PR already raised findings **F1–Fn** (each with its claim, file and status). The registry dedup is what keeps repeated rounds from minting duplicate threads for the same defect.

Answer the registry **before** raising anything new:

- **verify fixed** — the fixing hunk you can cite closes the finding: disposition `"fixed"` with the hunk reference. Never mark `fixed` without a citable hunk.
- **withdraw (reason required)** — the claim is wrong or no longer applies: disposition `"withdrawn"` with the reason. A withdrawal without a reason is rejected by the machine, and BLOCKING withdrawals surface to the owner.
- **mark re-introduced** — the defect is still there (e.g. the fix was reverted): leave the finding open and let your re-raise match it; do not re-litigate the claim from scratch.

New claims always need new evidence. A finding on the registry list is answered, not re-raised as if it were news — and the reviewer instruction stays maximally ambitious: raise every actionable finding you actually see.

**Candidates pending confirmation** (also listed in `pr_findings.md`): when a new finding you raised is *possibly same as F<n>*, the machine asks one word per candidate — confirm with `"same as F<n>"` or call it `"new"`. Unconfirmed candidates become new identities; nothing merges without your confirmation. This is a dedup request, not a push-back: confirming merges the threads, it does not weaken the finding (merges can only escalate severity, never de-escalate).

content.thinking:
So PR-review legs' input folders contain `pr_info.md`, `pr_diff.txt`, `pr_discussions.md` — no ticket.md. Story-development legs have `input/<KEY>/request.md` + `ticket.md` (like our input/gh-1334/).

The gh-1334 ticket is about the **PR review** path (reviewSpecClaims is used by postPReviewComments; postStoryTestAutomationReview also references it per grep? Actually the grep hit on test_postStoryTestAutomationReview* which tests... let me double check which files require reviewSpecClaims: js/postPReviewComments.js only (from the earlier grep list: js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js, js/postPReviewComments.js, tests). The test_postStoryTestAutomationReview hits were probably incidental (mentions in test descriptions or similar). Let me verify quickly later.

So the "ticket text" for the claim verification: the caller collects ticket-context texts available in the input folder: `ticket.md`, `request.md` (story-shaped folders). For PR-review legs those files often won't exist → verification unavailable → today's behavior + provenance 'inconclusive'. That matches the ticket's failure mode: "Ticket text unavailable in context: fall back today's behavior + provenance (never demote harder than today)."

Now let me also check where the PR review flow gets ticket text. In postPReviewComments, params.ticket is the Jira ticket object! `buildReviewContext` has `labels: ticketLabels(params.ticket)`. So the ticket object may be available: params.ticket.fields.description etc. But the module wants markdown text. Simplest deterministic source: read the input-folder files `ticket.md` and `request.md` via the inputFolderCandidates chain (like readPRInfoMarkdown does). Also fall back to `params.ticket` description? Let me keep it to input-folder files — that's exactly "the ticket text the review run already has (input/TICKET/)" per the ticket.

Now the round: the marker format `demoted-from-BLOCKING {round, reason: missing-citation, claimMatchedTicket: yes|no|inconclusive}`. Where does the caller get the round? The review-round number comes from the registry. In action(), sanitize runs before PR discovery. I'll make `round` optional in opts; postPReviewComments won't know it at sanitize time → marker carries `round: null`. Hmm, but the ticket explicitly wants round in the marker. Alternatively the marker could be stamped by the CALLER afterwards... that's complex.

Wait — actually let me reconsider. What posts the demoted thread? postInlineCommentsIfPresent posts reviewData.inlineComments[i].body (the demoted body with marker). The registry claim comes from resolveInlineComment → same body. So the marker in the body reaches both the posted thread AND the registry entry (via the claim text). For the registry entry the marker rides in the claim — the findingRegistry normalizeClaim strips punctuation, so marker words enter the claim word set. That slightly pollutes similarity but acceptable? The claim similarity between two rounds: round 1 finding cited (not demoted, no marker) vs round 2 same finding demoted (marker appended). Normalized claims differ by the marker words → similarity drops! E.g. claim "invalid login must return 401" (8 content words-ish) + marker words (~10 words: dmtools demoted from blocking round null reason missing citation claimatchedticket no) — that's a big dilution: overlap coefficient = 8ish/(8+10ish)... Both directions might fail candidate threshold 0.7. That would BREAK the dedup — the amnesia loop the ticket wants to close!

Better: keep the marker OUT of the claim text that goes into the registry. Options:

A. The registry findings derive claims from the ORIGINAL body (pre-sanitize). findingsFromReviewData runs after sanitize — could the marker be stripped there? The registry could strip machine markers from claims — normalizeClaim strips punctuation but keeps words.

B. Put the provenance into the finding object as a structured field instead of the body: sanitizeReviewData returns `demotions: [{ index/path/line, reason, claimMatchedTicket }]`; findingsFromReviewData attaches `demotion` to the finding; createIdentity stores it on the item; escalation packet surfaces it. The POSTED THREAD gets the textual marker in the body (fine — bodies aren't similarity-scored), but registry claims stay clean, and the registry entry gets the structured provenance.

B is cleaner and matches "stamps the posted thread AND the registry entry with a machine-parsed marker" — the registry entry carries it structured (machine-parsed by construction), the thread carries the HTML-comment marker.

But wait: the registry also reads the DEMOTED severity — the demoted finding enters the registry as IMPORTANT class. On a later round, if the same defect is re-raised WITH citation (BLOCKING), matchFinding auto-merge requires same severity class... `isAutoMerge` requires `severityClassOf(best.item.severity) === severity` — BLOCKING new finding vs IMPORTANT stored item → NOT auto-merge, becomes a candidate (same file + similarity ≥ threshold). The reviewer confirms "same as F<n>" → mergeIntoItem → escalateSeverity raises item to BLOCKING.

Hmm — AC5: "later round re-elevates the demoted finding by adding a citation instead of raising it as new." With B: the injection (`buildFindingsInjection`) lists F<n> as open with a demotion note; the reviewer re-raises with citation → candidate → confirm → escalate. That closes the loop. The severity-class mismatch only blocks AUTO-merge, not candidate+confirm. That's the existing deliberate design (invariant 1). Fine.

Now, does the demoted finding even enter the registry as an identity today? findingsFromReviewData maps ALL inlineComments (post-sanitize: severity IMPORTANT, body demoted). Yes — demoted findings register as IMPORTANT identities today already.

So the findingRegistry changes:
1. `finding` input shape: optional `demotion: { reason, claimMatchedTicket }` (round comes from the registry's own round bookeeping).
2. `createIdentity`: item.demotion = finding.demotion || null.
3. `queueCandidate`: candidates carry demotion too (a promoted candidate should keep provenance).
4. `mergeIntoItem`: if finding.demotion and no item.demotion → item.demotion = finding.demotion (first demotion provenance sticks; or update when the new one is different?). Keep first + history entry? Simplest: when a finding with demotion merges into an item without demotion, set it and push a history entry 'demotion-recorded'. Also when the item already has demotion and a cited re-raise escalates severity... provenance stays (history shows escalation).
5. `buildEscalationPacket`: add `demotions: [{n, id, file, severity, claim, reason, claimMatchedTicket}]` for items carrying demotion provenance.
6. `buildEscalationPacketComment`: render lines for demotions: "🚨?/⚠️ F<n> (<file>) demoted from BLOCKING (missing citation, claimMatchedTicket: no)".
7. `buildFindingsInjection`: for open items with demotion, append a hint: "F<n> was previously demoted from BLOCKING for a missing citation — if you re-raise it, include a verifiable citation and confirm 'same as F<n>' to re-elevate it."

Wait — but there's a subtlety: today, do demoted findings even reach findingsFromReviewData with their identity? Yes. And with the demotion provenance attached as a field, the registry item records it.

Now the reviewSpecClaims side:

```js
// ─ gh-1334: verify the claim against the ticket before demoting ─

var MIN_TICKET_ANCHOR_OVERLAP = 0.2;  // anchor match requires some requirement-word company
var TICKET_WORD_MATCH = 0.6;          // near-identical line: overlap coefficient
var MIN_CLAIM_WORDS_FOR_VERDICT = 3;  // below this the claim is too thin to judge 'no'

function quotedStringsOf(text) — /"([^"]{3,80})"|'([^']{3,80})'/g? Hmm, careful. Keep simple: double-quoted spans.
function anchorTokensOf(text) — numbers with 2+ digits + quoted strings (normalized lowercase)
function contentWordsOf(text) — reuse findingRegistry? reviewSpecClaims is standalone-pure with no requires. Should I require findingRegistry? The module header says "Pure module — no dmtools globals". requiring './findingRegistry.js' introduces a dependency — findingRegistry requires reviewVerdicts. Both are pure. Hoisted require at top — GralJS-safe (top-level require). But it couples modules; maybe reimplement a light normalization locally in reviewSpecClaims to keep it self-contained. The ticket says "normalization in the same style as #1332's claim normalization" — same STYLE, not the same module. A small local copy (normalize + stopwords-lite + stem-lite) risks divergence... but importing findingRegistry gives normalizeClaim + contentWords + claimSimilarity for free and they're exactly "the #1332 style". The pack require rules: hoist at top — fine. reviewVerdicts is required by findingRegistry — both pure modules, no dmtools globals. testRunner's loadModule(makeRequire({})) — let me check how makeRequire works for a module that requires siblings: loadModule('js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js', makeRequire({})) — makeRequire presumably builds a require that resolves relative to the module file. Let me check testRunner.js makeRequire.

/**
 * Sanitizes an agent's pr_review.json BEFORE the machine derives verdicts,
 * census, or posted bodies from it (gh-1053 machine-side guard, extended by
 * gh-1334).
 *
 * reviewData — the parsed pr_review.json object; mutated in place.
 * readText — OPTIONAL resolver for comment-file references
 *   (inlineComment.comment → markdown text); when omitted, file-referenced
 *   comments are inspected by their reference string only.
 * opts — OPTIONAL { trustedDocHosts: [...], ticketText, ticketFile, round }:
 *   trustedDocHosts overrides the default doc URL hosts accepted as
 *   citations; ticketText/ticketFile carry the ticket text the review run
 *   has (input/TICKET/) for gh-1334 verification; round (when known) is
 *   stamped into the demotion provenance marker.
 *
 * For every inline finding whose core claim is an uncited external-spec
 * assertion:
 *   - gh-1334: the claim verified against the ticket text — requirement
 *     present → severity kept BLOCKING and the matched citation (e.g.
 *     `ticket.md:3`) appended to the body (inline) or planned as a rewrite
 *     (comment file); census UNTOUCHED;
 *   - absent / inconclusive → severity field demoted to IMPORTANT;
 *   - every demotion stamps the body with the `dmtools:demoted-from-BLOCKING`
 *     marker and the inline entry with the structured `demotion` field;
 *   - inline bodies rewritten in place; file-referenced comments are NOT
 *     written here (pure module) — a rewrite { path, content } is returned
 *     for the caller to apply (once per physical comment file);
 *   - issueCounts rebalanced once per demoted comment (blocking −1,
 *     important +1, floor 0);
 *   - when no cited blocking finding remains, REQUEST_CHANGES/BLOCK
 *     collapses to APPROVE — matching the verdict-mapping table (no 🚨
 *     BLOCKING ⇒ APPROVE) so an uncited claim cannot arm rework.
 *
 * Returns { downgrades, census, notes, rewrites, demotions, citations } —
 * downgrades counts demoted findings, census the census moves applied
 * (≤ downgrades when one file is referenced twice), demotions the per-entry
 * provenance records, citations the keep-BLOCKING auto-appends; notes are
 * human-readable, observable in the workflow log.
 */
function sanitizeReviewData(reviewData, readText, opts) {
    var out = { downgrades: 0, census: 0, notes: [], rewrites: [], demotions: [], citations: [] };
    if (!reviewData) return out;

arguments.newText:
Without a verifiable citation:

- **Before emitting a spec-claim finding without a citation, locate the requirement in the ticket and cite it (for example `ticket.md:12`) — an uncited true claim is demoted mechanically.**
- Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `<source>` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking."
- Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`.

The machine applies the same discipline (and a safety net against coin-flip formatting): every uncited spec claim is cross-checked against the ticket text the run already has under `input/`. When the requirement is verifiably present there, the finding keeps 🚨 BLOCKING force and the matched citation is auto-appended; when the ticket contradicts it, lacks it, or the mechanical check is inconclusive, the finding is demoted and stamped `demoted-from-BLOCKING` — the finding-identity registry keeps it re-elevatable in a later round by adding a citation instead of raising the same defect as new.

This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force.

arguments.content:
### What changed
- `js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js` — before demoting an uncited spec claim, the demotion path now verifies the claim against the ticket text (`opts.ticketText`): requirement verifiably present → **keeps BLOCKING** and auto-appends the matched citation (`ticket.md:3`), census untouched; absent/inconclusive → demotes exactly as before. Matching is cheap and deterministic: gh-1332-style claim normalization, strong anchors (status codes like `401`, quoted strings) prioritized, anchor matches gated by requirement-word overlap.
- Every demotion now stamps the posted body with a machine-parsed `<!-- dmtools:demoted-from-BLOCKING {round, reason: missing-citation, claimMatchedTicket: yes|no|inconclusive} -->` marker and carries structured provenance on the inline entry.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js` — `applySpecClaimDowngrades` reads `ticket.md`/`request.md` along the input-folder candidate chain; the registry claim strips the machine-appended demotion tail and feeds the provenance into `js/common/findingRegistry.js`, which records it on the identity, surfaces demotions in escalation packets, and tells the next round how to re-elevate (cite + confirm "same as F<n>" → merge escalates back to BLOCKING).
- `instructions/pr_review/general_guidelines.md` — self-check sentence: locate the requirement in the ticket and cite it before emitting an uncited claim.

### Key decisions
- `yes`/`no`/`inconclusive` three-way verdict, biased to demote: never auto-escalates on a mismatch; no ticket text available → today's behavior + `inconclusive` provenance (never demotes harder than today).
- Registry provenance is structured (`item.demotion`), not marker-string-embedded; the machine-appended demotion note is stripped from registry claims so a cited re-raise still clears the candidate similarity bar (the gh-1332 amnesia loop closes).
- The demotion marker omits `round` when the sanitizer runs before the registry round is numbered; the registry item's own `history`/`rounds` carry the authoritative round.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_reviewSpecClaims.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_findingRegistry.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_postPRReviewComments.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # full suite: 8267 passed, 0 failed
```

All focused suites pass on the canonical runner (46 + 81 + 128). The work is complete and committed.

**Summary of what was done:**

- **Verification before demotion** (`js/common/reviewSpecClaims.js`): new `matchClaimInTicket()` compares an uncited spec claim against the ticket text using gh-1332-style normalization with strong-anchor priority (status codes, quoted strings) gated by requirement-word overlap. Present → keeps BLOCKING + auto-appends `ticket.md:NN`; absent/inconclusive → demotes exactly as today, never escalates.
- **Demotion provenance**: machine-parsed `dmtools:demoted-from-BLOCKING {round, reason, claimMatchedTicket}` marker on every demoted thread + structured provenance into the gh-1332 registry (`item.demotion`), escalation packets, and the next-round injection (cite + confirm → re-elevation via severity escalation).
- **Wiring** (`js/postPRReviewComments.js`): reads `ticket.md`/`request.md` along the input-folder chain; strips the machine-appended demotion tail from registry claims so cited re-raises clear the similarity bar.
- **Prompt-side prevention** (`instructions/pr_review/general_guidelines.md`): self-check sentence added.
- **Tests**: 67 new assertions across the three existing suites; full suite green via `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` (8267 passed, 0 failed).
